quest.title: Hereafter...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Primogem x20, Mora x20000

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: #You must be... {NICKNAME} and Paimon, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's us! We've got something very important to tell you, Earnshaw. But... let's talk about it later!

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: Just what kind of information is that mysterious... Fine, later it is.

talks.objective: Meet up with Lanoire and Caterpillar

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Look, that's your real home over there. It's just like Agnes described — at the breezy foothills of a mountain, upon a flowery field of grass.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: That's it...? It's just like Mom said...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon. Why don't you take Lanoire there?

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: What about you, Cater? Aren't you coming with us?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'm feeling pretty tired, so I'll rest up here for a while. I'll catch up with you later.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Then I'll stay with you. Once you're all rested up, we can go together.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME} and Ms. Paimon must be tired, too. It's a shame Bran and Mr. Wolsey aren't here...

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: ...I kinda wanna go back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Back where?

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Back to Meropide, of course!

choices.text: The Fortress of Meropide isn't your home.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't you want to go back to your real home, Lanoire? Look, you can see it from here. We just have to go over there, and we'll have reached the end of our adventure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And speaking of which, Paimon thinks we've met your family before. Now that she thinks about it, a lot of the details add up.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You explain how you helped Earnshaw find Prince, Princess, and Hero before...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Earnshaw's Tasses Ragout is soooo tasty! You're gonna love it, Lanoire!

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: It's just like Agnes said... Look, Lanoire, there's nothing to worry about. Go home, I know Earnshaw will take good care of you.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Will you go with me then, Cater? After you've rested?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Lanoire...

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Lanoire, everyone has somewhere they should return to. You should go back to your real home, and I have somewhere I should go, too.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Then... Then will we see each other again? At the end of the story, the characters in it all disappear... I don't think they see each other again...

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Of course we will. Your adventure is only just beginning, there's still a whole wide world out there for you to explore.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: This is just a temporary goodbye. We'll see each other again.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Really? Really, really? I know you've never lied to me before, but...

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Let me tell you a story, Lanoire.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Long, long ago... There was a mage's apprentice. He was a dim-witted apprentice, so it took him far more time than the others to learn the language of magic.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: But his teacher, who was an amazing mage, wasn't the least bit concerned. On the contrary, he heaped praise on his apprentice's progress, and even entrusted him with important tasks...

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: The apprentice never doubted his teacher's instructions. After all, he was a great mage who taught him the language of magic.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: The mage had a basin in his workshop. Actually, you could call it a fish bowl, as he kept a little fish in it.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: One day, the little fish called out to the apprentice: "Hey, you over there! Nitwit! Help me out."

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: The apprentice was taken aback. Apart from the great mage, nobody, or no creature even, would make conversation with him like that. So, this piqued his curiosity and he asked how he could help.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: As it turned out, this little fish used to live in the vast and boundless sea. By being brought here, it had been separated from its family. It had tried to ask others for help, but none had responded to it.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: "I'd like to bring you home, but my teacher has forbidden me from going out..." the apprentice said. Hearing this, the little fish swam crestfallen to the other side of the basin, saying nothing further to the apprentice.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Then one day, the apprentice discovered that the little fish was no longer in the basin. Who took it away? Did they bring it home? The apprentice couldn't help but wonder.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Without the little fish, the basin was now completely empty. Just what sort of place is the "vast and boundless sea"? Before he realized it, the apprentice's thoughts had drifted to the world outside the workshop...

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: And then what? I bet the mage's apprentice leaves the workshop!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: But the little fish... Did it go back to its home? The sea... That's a place with lots and lots of water, right? Does the apprentice find it?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: I'll tell you the rest of the story next time.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Awww!

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Only listening to my stories can't be that much fun.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: The next time we meet, if you don't want to hear my stories anymore, you could tell me some of the stories you hear from Earnshaw.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: I think he'll have many stories he'd like to share with you.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Well... then... the next time we meet, I'll be sure to have lots and lots of amazing stories to tell you...

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: I look forward to hearing them, too.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: For now, it's time for you to go home, Lanoire. This goodbye is only temporary, we'll see each other again.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Okay... then... until next time, Cater!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon... Let's go!

choices.text: Going back now probably wouldn't be a great idea.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right, getting out of there wasn't easy... Plus, if we go back now, Paimon thinks it would be bad news for Estienne and the others.

talks.objective: Meet up with Lanoire and Caterpillar
Bring Lanoire back to her family

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: Oh! What are you kids doing here? And this young lady is...

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: Strange... She looks rather like...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Together with Paimon, you describe to Earnshaw what you heard about Agnes from Caterpillar. As you speak, Lanoire supplements the tale with a few childish words of her own...

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: So that's what happened... That silly girl's already...

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Mother's not in Meropide. Is she not here either?

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: Yeah. She didn't like it here, so she left and never returned.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Why? This place is full of things she likes!

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: I recognized Prince, Princess, and Hero as soon as I saw them!

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Mom said that she was always very quick to change her mind, and she pestered her dad... Oh, I mean Grandpa, for ages until he finally agreed to get her puppies. She really liked dressing them up, but...

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: But soon she had something else she became even more fond of, so she didn't get to watch them grow up.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Why won't she come back? If she doesn't come back soon, I'm gonna grow up as well.

choices.text: She'll come back and see you grow up.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Really? But I thought she wasn't coming back because she found something she liked more...

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: So is this place going to be my home from now on?

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: That's right, child. This place is your home now...

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Okay... Mm, I smell Tasses Ragout!

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: You can eat as much as you'd like.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: ...I'm back in my own home now. This way, I think Cater will be happy too.

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: "Cater"... Is he the one who took care of her? If it's alright, could you invite him to rest a while here at the cabin?

choices.text: He's got other things to take care of.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: That's right. He knows a lot, so lots of people go to him for help.

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: Is that so? Well, that's a pity. Could you help me get a message to him then? No matter when, he will always be welcome here with open arms.

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: If you ever get the chance, invite him over to be our guest.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'll tell him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure thing, leave it to us.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Cater and I agreed that the next time we meet, I'm gonna tell many great stories to him...

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: Well, looks like we've got a lot of awesome stories to prepare, then. We can't be sharing stories with him that aren't at least a hundred times more incredible than his.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: ...Okay! A hundred times... Even Cater will be surprised!

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: We can reminisce about the old days while we drink tea and even enjoy some snacks...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're finally back in your real home, Lanoire. You must be tired. We'll leave you to it for now.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon, are you guys leaving too?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We've got our own adventures to go on.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Okay then... When I grow a little older, can we go on adventures together? Oh, and Cater can come along as well!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: #Okay... Thank you, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME} and Ms. Paimon. See you guys later!

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: You guys are leaving now? Thank you... Thank you guys... Safe journeys.

choices.text: We can discuss it when you're older.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: When we were in Meropide, he was really good at hide-and-seek! Nobody could find him if he really wanted to hide.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... He's quite shy, so he's watching us from a distance. As long as he knows Lanoire's home safe and sound, he'll be content.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Caterpillar... Wouldn't it be great to meet Grandpa Earnshaw and Lanoire right now? Are you sure about this?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: She's returned to a normal world with her real family. For her, I'd say things couldn't have ended any better.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: As for me... She'll forget about me in no time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, don't say that! You should know that you mean a lot to her too. She definitely won't forget the promise you two made to each other.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If you really never see her again, she will be heartbroken...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: She won't. Children tend to quickly forget both meetings and farewells. This is how they grow up.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'm simply a character in a story — brave at times, yet also an evil monster at others...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Let this fantastical story be a memory consigned to her past. She has the real world now, one that's hundreds of times better than any fantasy narrative.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, thank you.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: As I mentioned before, there are places better suited to retelling history, like the <color=#00E1FFFF>Narzissenkreuz Ordo...</color>

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like a very mysterious place... Where is it? How do we get there?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: It is very mysterious indeed. The outside world has changed so much over the centuries... which is why you may need to seek out a new way to the Narzissenkreuz Ordo.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aww, why does it have to be like that... Although, we are quite the adventurer duo, and we've been through it all! So wherever this historical ruins or mysterious place may be, it won't be a problem for us!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll find it for sure!

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Certainly. I will do what I can.

dialogues.text: You follow Caterpillar's directions to a secret path leading out of Fortress Meropide...

dialogues.text: Hmm... Never mind. My eyes must be getting worse with age.
